title: The Muscular System — Specific Muscles
prof_rule: his prof's material wins. this is reference depth.

naming_conventions.by_action: flexor, extensor, abductor, adductor, levator (lifts), depressor (lowers), supinator, pronator

muscle_interactions.agonist_prime_mover: the muscle primarily responsible for a movement. biceps brachii is agonist for elbow flexion.
muscle_interactions.antagonist: opposes the agonist. triceps brachii antagonizes biceps during elbow flexion. relaxes while agonist contracts.
muscle_interactions.synergist: assists the agonist. brachialis assists biceps in elbow flexion.
muscle_interactions.fixator: stabilizes the origin of the agonist so it can act efficiently. rotator cuff stabilizes shoulder while deltoid abducts arm.

lever_systems.components: fulcrum (joint), effort (muscle force), load (resistance/weight of body part + any external load)
lever_systems.first_class: fulcrum between effort and load. like a seesaw. EX: head nodding — atlanto-occipital joint is fulcrum, posterior neck muscles are effort, face/front of skull is load.
lever_systems.second_class: load between fulcrum and effort. like a wheelbarrow. RARE. EX: standing on tiptoes — toes are fulcrum, calf muscles (gastrocnemius) are effort, body weight is load.
lever_systems.third_class: effort between fulcrum and load. MOST COMMON in body. EX: biceps curl — elbow is fulcrum, biceps is effort, forearm/hand/weight is load. favors speed + range of motion over force.

facial_expression.note: all innervated by FACIAL NERVE (CN VII). insert into SKIN, not bone. that's why they move the face.

buccinator.action: compresses cheek (blowing, sucking, chewing — keeps food between teeth)

platysma.action: tenses neck skin, pulls corners of mouth down (frowning)

mastication.note: chewing muscles. innervated by TRIGEMINAL NERVE (CN V).

masseter.action: ELEVATES mandible (close jaw). strongest muscle in body by weight.

lateral_pterygoid.action: DEPRESSES + PROTRACTS mandible (opens jaw, juts chin forward)

sternocleidomastoid.action: ONE side: rotates head to OPPOSITE side + lateral flexion to SAME side. BOTH sides: flex neck (chin to chest). ACCESSORY NERVE (CN XI).
sternocleidomastoid.note: the name tells you everything. sterno + cleido + mastoid.

scalenes.action: elevate ribs (assist breathing), lateral flexion of neck

hyoid_muscles.suprahyoid: ABOVE hyoid. elevate hyoid + larynx during swallowing. digastric, mylohyoid, geniohyoid, stylohyoid.
hyoid_muscles.infrahyoid: BELOW hyoid. depress hyoid + larynx after swallowing. sternohyoid, omohyoid, sternothyroid, thyrohyoid.

pectoralis_major.action: flexes, adducts, medially rotates arm. main pushing muscle.

pectoralis_minor.action: protracts + depresses scapula. (deep to pec major)

serratus_anterior.action: protracts scapula (punching muscle). holds scapula against thoracic wall. weakness = winged scapula.

diaphragm.origin: inferior border of ribcage, xiphoid, lumbar vertebrae
diaphragm.action: PRIME MOVER of breathing. contracts → flattens → increases thoracic volume → air enters. PHRENIC NERVE.

internal_intercostals.action: depress ribs during FORCED EXPIRATION (compress ribcage)

abdominal_wall.note: four layers. fibers run in DIFFERENT DIRECTIONS for strength (like plywood). no bones in ventral trunk wall — muscles ARE the wall.

rectus_abdominis.action: flexes trunk (sit-ups). RECTUS = straight/vertical fibers. separated by tendinous intersections (six-pack lines) + linea alba (midline).

external_oblique.action: compress abdomen, flex + rotate trunk. fibers run INFERIOMEDIALLY (hands in pockets direction).

internal_oblique.action: same as external oblique. fibers run PERPENDICULAR to external oblique (upward fan).

transversus_abdominis.action: compresses abdomen (corset muscle). DEEPEST layer. fibers run HORIZONTALLY.

trapezius.action: elevates, retracts, depresses, rotates scapula (depends on which fibers). ACCESSORY NERVE (CN XI).

latissimus_dorsi.origin: spinous processes T7-L5, iliac crest, ribs 8-12
latissimus_dorsi.action: extends, adducts, medially rotates arm. WIDEST muscle. pull-ups, swimming strokes, lat pulldowns.

erector_spinae.what: THREE columns running vertically along spine: iliocostalis (lateral), longissimus (middle), spinalis (medial). action: extends + laterally flexes vertebral column. maintains posture. bilaterally = stand straight. unilaterally = side bend.

quadratus_lumborum.action: lateral flexion of trunk, fixes rib 12 during breathing

deltoid.action: anterior fibers: flex + medially rotate. middle fibers: ABDUCT arm. posterior fibers: extend + laterally rotate. MAIN abductor past first 15 degrees.

rotator_cuff_SITS.note: four muscles that stabilize the glenohumeral joint. mnemonic: S.I.T.S.

supraspinatus.action: INITIATES abduction (first 15 degrees). most commonly torn rotator cuff muscle.

biceps_brachii.origin: short head: coracoid process. long head: supraglenoid tubercle.
biceps_brachii.action: FLEXES elbow, SUPINATES forearm (turning doorknob), weak shoulder flexion.

brachialis.action: FLEXES elbow. actually the MAIN elbow flexor (not biceps). deeper than biceps.

triceps_brachii.origin: long head: infraglenoid tubercle. lateral + medial heads: posterior humerus.
triceps_brachii.action: EXTENDS elbow. antagonist of biceps. the only major elbow extensor.

forearm.note: MANY muscles. general rule: ANTERIOR = flexors (grip, wrist flexion). POSTERIOR = extensors (open hand, wrist extension). key ones:

iliopsoas.what: two muscles acting as one: iliacus + psoas major
iliopsoas.action: PRIME MOVER of hip flexion. brings thigh toward trunk. also flexes trunk toward thigh (sit-ups).

hip_flexors.rectus_femoris: also flexes hip (because it crosses BOTH hip and knee joints) — see quadriceps below

sartorius.action: flexes, abducts, laterally rotates thigh + flexes knee. LONGEST muscle in the body. cross-legged sitting muscle.

gluteus_maximus.insertion: gluteal tuberosity of femur + IT band
gluteus_maximus.action: EXTENDS + laterally rotates thigh. climbing stairs, standing from sitting. LARGEST muscle in body.

gluteus_medius.action: ABDUCTS thigh + medially rotates. stabilizes pelvis during walking (Trendelenburg sign if weak). INJECTION SITE.

hip_adductors.note: medial thigh compartment. all adduct the thigh.

adductor_magnus.action: adducts thigh. LARGEST adductor. anterior fibers flex, posterior fibers extend.

gracilis.action: adducts thigh + flexes knee. only adductor that crosses the knee.

quadriceps_anterior.note: FOUR muscles. all converge on the QUADRICEPS TENDON → patella → PATELLAR LIGAMENT → tibial tuberosity. ALL EXTEND THE KNEE.

rectus_femoris.action: extends knee + flexes hip (crosses both joints). only quad that does both.

vastus_lateralis.action: extends knee. LARGEST of the quad group. common injection site.

vastus_medialis.action: extends knee. VMO (vastus medialis oblique) stabilizes patella.

vastus_intermedius.action: extends knee. deepest quad, under rectus femoris.

hamstrings_posterior.note: THREE muscles. posterior thigh. all cross BOTH hip and knee. all extend hip + flex knee. innervated by SCIATIC NERVE.

biceps_femoris.origin: long head: ischial tuberosity. short head: linea aspera.
biceps_femoris.action: extends hip, flexes knee, laterally rotates leg.

semitendinosus.action: extends hip, flexes knee, medially rotates leg.

semimembranosus.action: extends hip, flexes knee, medially rotates leg.

tibialis_anterior.action: DORSIFLEXES foot + INVERTS foot. prime mover of dorsiflexion.

gastrocnemius.action: PLANTARFLEXES foot + flexes knee. the visible calf muscle. crosses both knee and ankle.

soleus.action: plantarflexes foot. deep to gastrocnemius. does NOT cross knee. postural muscle.

posterior_plantarflexors.note: gastrocnemius + soleus together = TRICEPS SURAE. both insert via achilles tendon.

lateral_evertors.note: older name: peroneus longus/brevis. fibularis is current.
